subtitle: How a single carved doorway kept Kamarupa’s vanished temples alive

panels.shot: low-angle dramatic wide of the ornate stone doorway rising from misty Assam hills at dawn
panels.action: Haruppeshvara Artisan, lean and weathered, stands in silhouette before the elaborately carved stone doorframe of Da Parbatiya, jungle and river mist curling around the lone surviving fragment of an ancient temple.

dialogue.text: In the flood-plains of ancient Kamarupa, where temples fell and capitals moved, one stone doorway at Da Parbatiya kept the forgotten hand of Haruppeshvara alive.

i18n.hi: प्राचीन कामरूप की बाढ़-मैदानों में, जहाँ मंदिर ढहे और राजधानियाँ बदलीं, दा पारबतिया का एक पत्थर दरवाज़ा हरुप्पेश्वर के भूले हाथ को ज़िंदा रखे रहा।

panels.shot: high bird’s-eye over the Brahmaputra valley, wide and winding, dotted with early medieval settlements
panels.action: The wide Brahmaputra snakes through dense forests and small clearings of thatched roofs and smoke, low hills rising near Tezpur as clouds cast moving shadows over an early medieval landscape.

dialogue.text: To understand the stone door, we must first see its land: Kamarupa, on the banks of the restless Brahmaputra, between forested hills and shifting sands.

i18n.hi: इस पत्थर दरवाज़े को समझने के लिए, पहले उसकी धरती देखें: कामरूप, बेचैन ब्रह्मपुत्र के किनारे, जंगल भरी पहाड़ियों और खिसकती रेतों के बीच।

panels.shot: slow push-in toward a small hill settlement near Tezpur, with a shrine site marked by bamboo poles and stones
panels.action: On a low hill near the river, villagers gather around a sacred clearing marked by rough stones and bamboo flags, smoke of incense curling, as elders gesture toward the slope where a future temple will stand.

dialogue.text: Near the place later called Tezpur, people came to a hill they knew as sacred long before kings wrote its name into copper and stone.

i18n.hi: जहाँ बाद में तेजपुर कहलाया, वहाँ लोग उस पहाड़ी पर आते थे जिसे वे राजाओं के ताम्रपत्रों से बहुत पहले से पवित्र मानते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of the artisan examining a rough stone block, sunlight catching the dust
panels.action: Haruppeshvara Artisan, young and focused, runs his hand over a freshly quarried stone block, eyes narrowing as he imagines lines and figures hidden beneath the rough surface.

dialogue.text: Somewhere in the 6th or 7th century, an artisan of Haruppeshvara took such stone in his hands and saw not weight, but a door for gods and humans.

i18n.hi: छठी–सातवीं सदी के कहीं, हरुप्पेश्वर के एक शिल्पी ने ऐसा पत्थर हाथ में लिया और उसमें बोझ नहीं, देवों और मनुष्यों के लिए दरवाज़ा देखा।

panels.shot: close-up on chisel meeting stone, chips flying in a frozen moment
panels.action: In a frozen instant, Haruppeshvara Artisan’s chisel bites into the stone, a sharp flake caught mid-air as his steady hand guides the first groove of a future pattern.

dialogue.text: He had seen carvings from far to the west, heard of new styles moving along trade paths, yet his river, his forests, his deities demanded their own forms.

i18n.hi: वह पश्चिम की दूर की नक्काशियाँ देख चुका था, व्यापार-पथों से आती नई शैलियाँ सुन चुका था, पर उसकी नदी, उसके जंगल, उसके देव अपने रूप माँगते थे।

panels.shot: wide shot of a workshop scene with multiple partially carved blocks, the doorway vertical in the center
panels.action: Inside a simple open-air workshop, several stone blocks lie at different stages of carving, while the central uprights and lintel of a doorway rise together, the Haruppeshvara Artisan perched on a platform, chiseling intricate figures.

dialogue.text: In that workshop near Haruppeshvara, pillars, lintels and images grew day by day. This doorframe was not a lone masterpiece, but part of a living craft tradition.

i18n.hi: हरुप्पेश्वर के पास उस कार्यशाला में रोज़–रोज़ स्तंभ, ऊपर की बलियाँ और छवियाँ उभरती रहीं। यह चौखट अकेली कला-कृति नहीं, जीवित शिल्प परंपरा का हिस्सा थी।

panels.shot: medium close-up of the artisan carving a divine figure on the jamb, intent and reverent
panels.action: Haruppeshvara Artisan, sweat beading on his brow, carefully shapes the face of a deity on the side jamb, his lips slightly parted as if murmuring a silent prayer while he perfects the gentle curve of the cheek.

dialogue.speaker: Haruppeshvara Artisan
dialogue.text: Stone remembers what the river forgets.

i18n.hi: पत्थर वह सब रख लेता है जो नदी भूल जाती है।

panels.shot: low-angle of the nearly finished doorway lying on the ground, artisan and helpers around
panels.action: The nearly complete doorframe, richly carved with scrolls and figures, lies horizontal on wooden supports as Haruppeshvara Artisan and a few helpers study it, the sky a bright strip above them.

dialogue.text: When the carving was done, the door lay on the earth, a frame for an opening that was not yet there. Its final place would be a temple now lost to the ground and the river.

i18n.hi: नक्काशी पूरी हुई तो दरवाज़ा ज़मीन पर ही पड़ा रहा, ऐसे द्वार की चौखट जो अभी बना ही नहीं था। उसकी आख़िरी जगह वह मंदिर था जो अब धरती और नदी के नीचे खो गया है।

panels.shot: wide shot of the doorway being raised into position amid scaffolding at a hilltop temple site
panels.action: On a terraced hillside, bamboo scaffolding surrounds a low stone platform as workers strain with ropes to lift the heavy, carved frame upright, Haruppeshvara Artisan guiding them with raised, tense hands.

dialogue.text: Carefully they raised the frame at a hill-site near Tezpur, making a threshold not just for a shrine, but for an entire style of early medieval Assam.

i18n.hi: सावधानी से उन्होंने चौखट को तेजपुर के पास एक पहाड़ी पर खड़ा किया, यह दहलीज़ सिर्फ़ एक देवालय की नहीं, असम के आरंभिक मध्यकालीन अंदाज़ की भी बन गई।

panels.shot: time-lapse style composite, the temple structure suggested in silhouette behind the door as years pass
panels.action: Behind the now-standing doorway, the vague silhouette of a shrine roof appears and fades, villagers come and go with offerings, then all blur into ghostly trails as the hill is slowly reclaimed by trees.

dialogue.text: We do not know the full temple that rose behind it, nor the king who funded it. Its name is silent in stone; only the doorway speaks clearly.

i18n.hi: हम न उस पूरे मंदिर को जानते हैं जो इसके पीछे उठा, न उस राजा को जिसने धन दिया। उसका नाम पत्थर में चुप है; साफ़–साफ़ तो बस यह चौखट बोलती है।

panels.shot: dramatic shot of storm clouds over the Brahmaputra, with waves battering its banks
panels.action: Dark monsoon clouds roll low over the swollen Brahmaputra as waves slam into its eroding banks, trees tilting and falling into the flood while distant lightning forks over the valley.

dialogue.text: In this valley, rivers shifted course, embankments failed, floods swallowed villages. What was stone yesterday could be silt today.

i18n.hi: इस घाटी में नदियाँ रास्ता बदलती रहीं, बाँध टूटते, बाढ़ें गाँव निगलती रहीं। जो कल पत्थर था, वह आज कीचड़ हो सकता था।

panels.shot: low wide shot of the hill during an earthquake, stones shifting and dust rising
panels.action: The temple hill shudders as an unseen earthquake ripples through, loose stones tumbling, cracks running through old masonry while dust clouds rise into the air.

dialogue.text: Earthquakes shook Assam again and again across centuries, breaking walls, toppling shrines. Each tremor edited the landscape and the record of its builders.

i18n.hi: भूकंप सदियों से बार–बार असम को झकझोरते रहे, दीवारें तोड़ीं, मंदिर गिराए। हर झटके ने ज़मीन और उसके निर्माताओं की याद में काट–छाँट कर दी।

panels.shot: wide shot of ruined stones and a leaning doorway fragment amid new vegetation
panels.action: Among toppled blocks and scattered fragments half-buried in soil and grass, the carved doorway leans but still stands, creepers beginning to wind around its figures as saplings sprout nearby.

dialogue.text: Yet the door endured. Roofs collapsed, halls vanished, but the carved frame held, its weight and design somehow aligned with survival.

i18n.hi: फिर भी यह दरवाज़ा बचा रहा। छतें गिरीं, सभागृह गायब हुए, पर नक्काशीदार चौखट टिक गई, उसका वज़न और बनावट जैसे बचने के साथ ताल में थी।

panels.shot: transition shot showing centuries passing, with styles of clothing changing around the silent doorway
panels.action: The doorway stands unchanged while around it figures in different dress and ornaments flicker past through time—early medieval, later medieval, early modern—each generation smaller and more uncertain around the ancient stone.

dialogue.text: Over centuries, power shifted to new dynasties like the Salastambhas, who left copper plates naming places like Tezpur and Haruppeshvara, while the old door quietly outlived their courts.

i18n.hi: सदियों में सत्ता सलस्तंभ जैसे नए वंशों तक पहुँची, जिन्होंने तेजपुर और हरुप्पेश्वर जैसे नामों वाले ताम्रपत्र छोड़े, जबकि पुराना दरवाज़ा चुपचाप उनके दरबारों से भी अधिक जीता रहा।

panels.shot: close-up of a copper plate inscription being read by a later scribe, the doorway faint in the background
panels.action: A scribe in later times bends over a gleaming copper plate, its inscription lines crisp, while through the open window behind him the faint outline of a distant hill and the lone doorway can be glimpsed.

dialogue.text: The Hayunthal, Tezpur and Parbatiya plates spoke of grants, rulers and sacred geography. Together with the door, they let historians trace a kingdom that floods and time had almost erased.

i18n.hi: हयुंथल, तेजपुर और पारबतिया की ताम्रपट्टिकाएँ अनुदानों, शासकों और पवित्र भूगोल की बातें करती रहीं। दरवाज़े के साथ मिलकर उन्होंने इतिहासकारों को वह राज्य चुनने दिया जिसे बाढ़ और समय ने लगभग मिटा दिया था।

panels.shot: archaeological wide shot in the 19th–20th century, scholars and workers around the doorway taking measurements
panels.action: Modern-era archaeologists and local workers stand around the doorway with measuring tapes and notebooks, one pointing out a carved motif while another carefully sketches the jamb’s figures.

dialogue.text: When scholars and the Archaeological Survey of India studied Da Parbatiya, they saw in this frame one of the finest surviving pieces of early medieval temple art in Assam.

i18n.hi: जब विद्वानों और भारतीय पुरातत्व सर्वेक्षण ने दा पारबतिया को देखा, उन्होंने इस चौखट में असम की आरंभिक मध्यकालीन मंदिर-कला के सबसे सुंदर बचे नमूनों में एक को पहचाना।

panels.shot: poetic cross-time shot: the artisan’s ghostly figure overlapped with a modern archaeologist tracing the carvings
panels.action: The faint, transparent image of Haruppeshvara Artisan stands overlaying a modern researcher who gently traces a carved figure on the doorframe, their hands aligned across the centuries.

dialogue.text: Through their notes, drawings and photographs, the artisan’s forgotten decisions—how to place a curve, how to balance a figure—entered the language of Indian art history.

i18n.hi: उनकी टिप्पणियों, रेखाचित्रों और तस्वीरों से उस शिल्पी के भूले फ़ैसले—कहाँ मोड़ रखना, कैसे आकृति सँभालनी—भारतीय कला इतिहास की भाषा का हिस्सा बन गए।

panels.shot: tight close-up on a section of the carving: stylised figures and scrollwork, weathered yet sharp
panels.action: A detailed view of the doorframe’s carvings fills the frame—elegant figures seated within arches, flowing scrollwork and geometric bands, edges softened by age but still precise and ordered.

dialogue.text: Scholars read in its lines a blend of wider Indian motifs and local taste, early evidence that Kamarupa’s craftsmen were part of a shared yet distinct sacred art.

i18n.hi: विद्वानों ने इसकी रेखाओं में व्यापक भारतीय रूपकों और स्थानीय स्वाद का संगम पढ़ा, यह शुरुआती सबूत कि कामरूप के शिल्पी साझा, फिर भी अलग, पवित्र कला के हिस्सेदार थे।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of the doorway standing alone on the hill at sunset, valley and river beyond
panels.action: At sunset, the Da Parbatiya doorway stands alone on its hill, the Brahmaputra glinting in the far distance, sky burning orange as long shadows stretch from the weathered stone into the valley.

dialogue.text: Most of Haruppeshvara’s temples are now emptiness and memory, yet this single stone door shows that even a fragment can hold an entire civilization’s hand in ours.

i18n.hi: हरुप्पेश्वर के ज़्यादातर मंदिर अब खालीपन और स्मृति हैं, पर यह अकेला पत्थर दरवाज़ा दिखाता है कि एक टुकड़ा भी पूरी सभ्यता का हाथ हमारे हाथ में थमा सकता है।

title_i18n.en: The Stone Door at Da Parbatiya
title_i18n.hi: दा पारबतिया का पत्थर वाला दरवाज़ा

subtitle_i18n.en: How a single carved doorway kept Kamarupa’s vanished temples alive
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक नक्काशीदार चौखट ने कामरूप के खोए मंदिरों को ज़िंदा रखा
